title: Tribunal administratif widens force majeure doctrine in flood-liability arrêt
content: The Tribunal administratif d’Aurelle ruled on Tuesday that repeated flooding in the Vallonne valley can no longer be treated as unforeseeable, in an *arrêt de principe* that restricts the use of force majeure by insurers and redefines the liability of municipalities in at-risk zones.

The case was brought by 1,340 households whose properties were flooded three times between 2016 and 2024. Their insurers had refused compensation on the ground that the second and third floods fell within the force majeure exception, as each event exceeded the levels recorded in the official mapping of the basin.

The court rejected that reasoning. A risk that has materialised three times in eight years cannot be characterised as “<u>imprévisible</u>” merely because each occurrence exceeded earlier records, the judgment states; the doctrine of force majeure presupposes an event that a diligent operator could not have anticipated, not an intensification of a known hazard.

The decision orders the insurers to compensate at the contractual level and refers the question of the municipalities’ share of the cost to a separate proceeding. Preliminary estimates put the total exposure at 220 million livres, though the Fédération des assureurs des Républiques said on Wednesday that the figure was “materially overstated”.

The federation has announced an appeal to the Conseil d’État, arguing that the arrêt effectively makes insurers the guarantors of climate change and will force a repricing of premiums across the eastern republics. Consumer groups countered that premiums have already risen by an average of 31 per cent since 2021 without any improvement in settlement times.

Legal scholars described the judgment as the most significant shift in administrative doctrine on natural hazards in a decade, while noting that the Conseil d’État has previously narrowed expansive readings of liability when the budgetary consequences became clear.

A government study on climate adaptation finance, due in December, is expected to address the question of a public reinsurance mechanism for the most exposed basins. The Ministry of Finance has declined to comment on the judgment before the appeal is lodged.
author: Inès Rouvier, chronique judiciaire — Presses de Vallonne
